title: Pop the Hood on Your Heart
excerpt: Ever ignore the check engine light? Proverbs 4:23 is an engine manual for your soul. A heart tune-up in four verses, three questions, two truths and one step.
author: TheWrkShop Team
source_note: Unsent Kit draft (Jul 25, 2025), shaped into the full 4-3-2-1 format Nov 2026. Unlisted bonus page.
body_html: The WorkShop Happy 4-3-2-1 Weekend Edition · Bonus
Bro, when was the last time you popped the hood on your heart?

Ever ignore the check engine light in your car?
It doesn’t end well.
Same with your heart and mind. Proverbs 4:23 says:
“Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.”
That’s not spiritual poetry, that’s an engine manual for your soul.
Because if your spiritual engine is misfiring, everything sputters: relationships, decisions, peace, joy, purpose.
This weekend, let’s give our hearts a tune-up so we’re not stuck on the side of life’s highway.

One-Minute Win of the Week
Pray this right now: “Lord, pop the hood on my heart. Search me, clean me, and tune me up for Your purpose. I don’t want to drive another mile with my spiritual engine light on. In Jesus’ name, Amen.”
4 Verses to Pop the Hood On
“Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.”
Insight: Guard your heart, because EVERYTHING flows from it.
Gem: Whatever is running your heart is driving your life.
“Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts. See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.”
Insight: Invite God to run a diagnostic scan.
Gem: You can’t fix what you won’t let Him find.
“Whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable… think about such things.”
Insight: Filter what fuel you’re putting in.
Gem: Cheap fuel always costs more down the road.
“They have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug their own cisterns, broken cisterns that cannot hold water.”
Insight: Stop digging broken cisterns and drink living water instead.
Gem: Broken cisterns run dry right when you need them most.
3 Questions for Your Heart Scan
• Where’s my “check engine light” blinking right now?
• What spiritual carbon buildup have I been ignoring?
• Am I running my life on God’s power, or my own fumes?
2 Truths to Keep Your Engine Running
• Small leaks become big breakdowns. Don’t ignore the little stuff.
• God’s tune-up always leads to more power, peace, and purpose.

Run a 10-Minute Heart Scan. Find a quiet spot, no phone. Read Psalm 139:23–24 slowly, twice. Ask God to show you one warning light. Write it down. Then fix one small leak today: a call you owe, a habit you’ve excused, a conversation you’ve been avoiding.

Drop the Mic Moment
“If you wouldn’t drive your truck with the check engine light on… why are you trying to drive your life that way?”
